designIntentSource.title: The different lightspeed methods
designIntentSource.role: Governing design intent for differentiated gravity sensitivity, miscalculation loss, predictive sensing, emergency de-transit, maturity-scaled safety, and separate technical development for nine transit methods.

purpose: Define family-specific emergency response machinery, stage ownership, physically admissible response models, signatures, scaling questions, failure cascades and generator requirements that can be translated into the generic dynamic escape envelope without flattening the nine transit families into one abort mechanism.
invariants: Transit family is supplied by family authority and never inferred from species, manufacturer, machinery style or source adjective.
Family response profiles define what physical machinery may control an emergency stage; they do not invent current measurements or numerical performance.
A family profile may supply an equation form only when its variables correspond to an explicitly modeled physical state.
No family receives a universal damage multiplier, technology-tier multiplier, species multiplier or fixed abort duration.
Continuous projected-progress, PRECOMMIT and PORTAL_ADMISSION families retain distinct route semantics.
Stored field energy, available sink power, deliverable bus power, thermal reserve and actuator slew are independent constraints.
A family response packet may increase a certified stage time or render it unresolved/blocked; it may not improve a certified stage time without stronger recertification authority.
Signatures are consequences of modeled machinery state and energy flow; they are not arbitrary stealth modifiers.
Race-specific embodiments may change hardware realization and evidence channels without changing family equations unless a narrower authority says otherwise.

commonModels.energyTransfer: t >= E_required / P_available for E_required > 0 and P_available > 0
commonModels.linearSlew: t >= abs(delta_q) / qdot_available for an explicitly defined bounded-rate state variable q
commonModels.translationImpulse: t >= m * abs(delta_v) / F_available under an approximately constant available force
commonModels.rotationImpulse: t >= I * abs(delta_omega) / tau_available under an approximately constant available torque
commonModels.thermalHold: t_hold = C_th * (T_limit - T_0) / (P_heat - P_reject) only for positive net heating and a valid lumped short-transient approximation
commonModels.brakingDistance: d_required >= v_upper * t_latency_upper + v_upper^2 / (2 * a_available_lower) for approximately constant positive deceleration authority
commonModels.explicitBound: Use an explicitly measured/certified upper response time when internal state-variable modeling is unavailable or inappropriate.

inertial-torch.responseConcept: Detect, decide, cut or redirect thrust, establish available deceleration/avoidance authority, execute ordinary-space impulse, clear the collision or thermal/structural hazard, and stabilize the vehicle.

clear: hazard miss distance or stopping clearance

scalingQuestions: propellant or reaction-mass reserve where applicable

metric-compression.responseConcept: Stop increasing the metric field, rebalance field-former sectors, remove stored field energy through certified sinks, restore a traversable unwind geometry, collapse or relax the compression state, then verify local-space recovery.

clear: local metric recovery and field-energy decay

scalingQuestions: number and spacing of field-former sectors
stored field energy under the selected model
signatures: rapid external lensing/metric-signature change if established by route physics
failureModes: thermal hold shorter than unwind time

gravitational-plane.responseConcept: Localize the shear fork or tidal-branch loss, reduce or redirect coupling to the active gravitational plane, slew/cancel coupling machinery within certified authority, detach before branch separation becomes destructive, and recover in a locally admissible state.
scalingQuestions: coupled vessel mass/volume if family authority requires it
number and geometry of coupling stations
signatures: attitude or structural-load transient during imperfect detach
failureModes: coupling cannot slew before branch separation

slipstream-shear.responseConcept: Detect boundary/adhesion deterioration, reduce or redistribute adhesion, open a certified detachment path, shed or sink stored coupling energy, cross the boundary under controlled authority, and clear the unstable shear region.

q-lattice.responseConcept: Freeze or invalidate the pending address/reference state before commitment, halt lattice transition sequencing, discharge or quarantine transition machinery, preserve a certified local reference, and verify that no partially committed address state remains active.
scalingQuestions: stored transition energy if explicitly modeled

n-manifold.responseConcept: Reject an invalid embedding before commitment, preserve the local chart/reference, close or unwind the embedding machinery through an authority-defined sequence, verify a valid return map, and prevent partial topology state from being treated as a completed transit.
scalingQuestions: number of controlled embedding degrees of freedom
failureModes: solver fails to converge within commit window

fold-jump.responseConcept: Reject the endpoint solution before fold commitment, stop closure sequencing, unload or sink fold-former energy through certified paths, reopen or retain the local geometry as required by the family authority, and confirm endpoint/emergence state never became committed.

phase-displacement.responseConcept: Preserve whole-object reference integrity, halt additional displacement before commitment, reverse or reconcile only through an explicitly certified family sequence, restore all protected components to one compatible reference state, and verify complete object coverage.

actuate: displacement-state slew only where explicitly modeled

scalingQuestions: energy transfer only where source authority defines it
signatures: reconciliation energy transient only if physically established

wormhole-gate.responseConcept: Stop new admission, preserve mouth synchronization long enough for occupied aperture clearance, reject or hold traffic according to certified policy, reduce or close aperture through bounded machinery, dispose of throat/field energy through certified sinks, and verify both mouths and exit volume are safe.

exit: admission termination or controlled aperture closure

arnock.baseline: Solid-state electromechanical modular technology with silicon computation, deterministic sectional control, integrated functional modules and piezoelectric condition/alignment instrumentation.
implementationNotes: Map family response functions onto replaceable field, converter, actuator, sensor and control modules rather than generic biological organs.
Piezoelectric instrumentation may establish actuator/alignment/structural response but does not become gravity, topology, endpoint or Q-state sensing without specific sensor authority.
Module replacement may alter timing, calibration, heat load or field response and therefore can invalidate a previous family-response certificate.

zwlei-murrek.baseline: Fluidic/vane transit machinery using field vanes, hydraulic authority, dielectric fluid, bio-reactive power fluid, conductive coolant, Navigation Current reference systems and Sensor Choir/Forward Sensor Ampulla evidence where source authority supports them.
implementationNotes: Translate family response into vane slew, fluid delivery, hydraulic pressure/flow, dielectric integrity, coolant reserve and reference/sensor response when those variables are actually applicable.
The source phrase gravitic slipstream is preserved as source terminology and does not select gravitational-plane or slipstream-shear family identity.

generatorRules: Resolve canonical family first through familyMap.
Select the family profile but do not synthesize missing physical measurements.
For each required emergency stage, prefer current measured bounds, then certified family-response bounds, then explicit unresolved status.
Emit generic dynamic-escape stageModels only from an admissible family model whose variables are present and dimensionally compatible.
Preserve raw family evidence and provenance beside normalized stageModels.
Never assign a continuous projected velocity to PRECOMMIT or PORTAL_ADMISSION families.
Never convert a descriptive failure probability into time, distance, power, energy or actuator authority without an explicit physical mapping.
Never convert technology maturity directly into a numerical response multiplier; maturity may justify additional sensors, redundancy or narrower certified uncertainty only through evidence.
provenanceRule: Every generated family-response packet must preserve the canonical family, profile version, raw machinery evidence, selected response equations, generated dynamic-escape stage models, unresolved requirements, warnings and upstream authority references.
